items.title: Two ships scrapped for parts have suddenly reappeared in the Strait of Hormuz
items.description: Iran has effectively blocked the only way out of the Persian Gulf, leaving about 3,000 ships stranded. But two zombie ships appear to have sailed in and out of the Gulf through the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Trump says US and Iran 'want deal' as Tehran calls claim of talks 'fake news'
items.description: Donald Trump says there have been "major points of agreement" in US-Iran talks to end the war. But Iran denies those claims.

items.title: TACO Trump strikes again with sudden Iran backdown
items.description: After threatening to "obliterate" Iran's power plants, Donald Trump's sudden backdown is again fuelling TACO taunts.

items.title: Yet another fuel shock proves renewables are a matter of national security
items.description: From UN leaders to former Australian Defence Force chiefs, a growing chorus of voices argues that dependence on fossil fuels is not just a climate issue, but a national security risk — exposing countries to volatile prices and supply shocks.

items.title: Fuel costs forcing potential 'life and death' decisions for rural patients
items.description: The Rural Doctors Association says some patients may be forced to make "life and death" decisions due to the rising cost of fuel in regional Australia.

items.title: Aged care algorithm 'like Russian roulette'
items.description: A new algorithm for deciding how much aged care support people can receive to stay living at home is being blamed for reducing care to older Australians.

items.title: 'Prioritised institution over students': Top university savaged
items.description: University of Technology Sydney (UTS) has been warned over "reprisal" action against a student who highlighted the university's failure to act on reviews into its gender-based violence policies.

items.title: Disillusioned voters back truth in political advertising reform
items.description: Civic groups are calling for sweeping reforms to restore falling trust, which experts have linked to a resurgence of populist "protest" voting at the expense of the major parties.

items.title: 'Here if you need': Ashton Hurn played a short and difficult game in the SA election
items.description: Sport and politics are similar. Good players work hard and perform well under pressure, something SA Liberal Leader Ashton Hurn has been credited for. But the party's disastrous election results show just how difficult the game can be.

items.title: Thousands of Victorian teachers and support staff strike amid pay dispute
items.description: About 500 state schools could close or face significant disruptions today, as teachers walk off the job for the first time in 13 years, says the Australian Education Union.

items.title: 'Moby Dick' whales headbutting captured on video for first time
items.description: Historic accounts dating back two centuries detail ships rammed and sunk by sperm whales, now scientists claim to have filmed the species for the first time displaying headbutting behaviour.

items.title: Australia and European Union to sign free trade agreement decades in the making
items.description: An EU trade agreement almost a decade in the making looks set to be signed but some industry groups are not happy.

items.title: MPs push gambling ad ban as study reveals targeting of women
items.description: Gambling is being promoted as fun, social and "harmless" for women through social media and lifestyle marketing, in a shift researchers warn is normalising betting and obscuring the risks.

items.title: Farmers sound alarm over imminent food price shocks
items.description: Australia's peak farming body is warning consumers the price of groceries is about to jump as producers and the freight industry grapple with diesel price hikes and supply issues.

items.title: Buying a share of my in-laws' home helped us into the property market
items.description: Experts say housing affordability is pushing people to rethink the rule book on property ownership.

items.title: Quiz: Are your maths skills sharper than a Year 9 student's?
items.description: Aussie students have just been put to the test with NAPLAN. Now it's your turn to see how you'd go in their shoes.

items.title: Take back some time in the morning with these make-ahead breakfasts
items.description: From breakfast sandwiches to chia pudding, these delicious morning options can be prepared ahead for a stress-free start to the day.

items.title: Ambulances set on fire in suspected antisemitic hate crime in London
items.description: Footage posted on social media appears to show three hooded people pouring gasoline on the vehicles before leaving the scene.

items.title: New Hong Kong law forces people to surrender passwords — or face jail
items.description: People in Hong Kong now face a year in jail if they refuse to hand over their phone or computer passwords to police.

items.title: Pyne and Downer weigh in on Liberal SA wipe-out, Greens increase vote
items.description: Former senior Liberals Christopher Pyne and Alexander Downer have weighed in on the disastrous state election result, calling for factions to work together. Meanwhile, the Greens have increased their primary vote.

items.title: As One Nation's vote soars, SA supporters explain their reasons
items.description: Heading into the South Australian election, One Nation was backing its chances to pick up votes from across the political spectrum, and supporters say various factors informed their decisions.

items.title: Nine seats to watch as counting continues after the SA election
items.description: ABC chief elections and data analyst Casey Briggs looks at what seats are still in doubt in the South Australian state election, as One Nation makes it into the final two candidates in the count in most of the state's 47 electorates.

items.title: Two dead after Air Canada jet collides with fire truck at New York airport
items.description: The pilot and copilot were killed after the plane struck the fire truck at a speed of about 39 kilometres per hour.

items.title: World energy watchdog warns fuel crisis is 'very severe'
items.description: World leaders have failed to grasp the depth of the energy crisis created by the Iran war, the head of the International Energy Agency has warned, as he considers releasing extra emergency oil stores.

items.title: 170 e-bike riders fined in blitz cracking down on 'silly, dangerous' behaviour
items.description: More than 300 e-bike riders have been stopped, including e-scooter riders, during an ongoing police operation in the Sutherland Shire.
